title: The Busy Leader: Healthy Eating and Enhanced Productivity
author: Heather McGonigal
summary: Coach Heather McGonigal of Leadership With a Twist treats healthy eating as a leadership fundamental and deliberately sets aside the diet debates about what and when to eat. Her working definition is simple: whatever helps a leader feel well, function well, and have the energy their life requires. The core move is to locate the real failure point not in knowledge but in busy weeks, when long meetings and working lunches replace good choices with the quickest ones. She therefore reframes self-care as planning ahead, making the supportive choice easier for one's future self through small decisions made in advance. The piece also rejects perfectionism, recommending curiosity over judgment with a short set of reflective questions, and ends with an invitation to prepare for one specific busy day.
points: Healthy habits usually collapse not when life is calm but when the calendar fills and the quickest option wins by default.
Self-care is recast as a design problem: reduce friction in advance so the supportive choice is easier for your future self.
One meal no more defines health than one workout defines fitness; the pattern of choices you return to is what matters.
Replacing self-judgment with curious questions about energy and effect produces information that leads to better decisions.
quotes: Because here is where things often fall apart: not when life is calm, but when life gets busy.

The calendar fills up. Meetings run long. You are working through lunch. You get home tired and realize you have nothing prepared. Suddenly, the choice you might normally make gets replaced by whatever is quickest and easiest.
It is not just about knowing what makes you feel good. It is about making that choice easier for your future self.

One meal does not define your health any more than one workout defines your fitness. What matters more is the overall relationship you are building with yourself and the choices you return to over time.
That kind of curiosity gives you useful information. And useful information helps you make better decisions.
Taking good care of yourself does not have to be complicated. Sometimes it is simply about making the supportive choice a little easier to reach.
